questions.question_text: The kappa statistic is commonly used to assess agreement across raters. Values above what number are considered to represent high levels of agreement?
questions.explanation: Values in the range of 0.40 to 0.75 represent moderate levels of agreement, and values below 0.40 represent low levels of agreement.

questions.question_text: Four categories of techniques are generally employed in the child psychiatric interview, which include engagement, projective, direct questioning, and interactive techniques. Which of the following describes projective techniques?

options.text: Techniques to clarify particular points or to elicit specific information
Techniques to put the child at ease so that the child will provide accurate and meaningful clinical information
Techniques to clarify how the child relates to as well as accepts or integrates input from others
Techniques to allow the child to reveal underlying themes or issues that the child may be unable to verbalize directly

correct_answer.text: Techniques to allow the child to reveal underlying themes or issues that the child may be unable to verbalize directly

correct_answers.text: Techniques to allow the child to reveal underlying themes or issues that the child may be unable to verbalize directly

questions.question_text: A 4-year-old boy displays extreme sadness and distress when he must say good-bye to his preschool teacher at the end of the school year. Which of the following would be most helpful in the transition?

options.text: Preventing any further contact between the boy and his teacher in the future
Introducing the boy to his next, new teacher right away
Reassuring the boy that he will have many teachers in the future
Telling the boy that his teacher left because of his bad behavior
Visiting with the preschool teacher after the farewell

correct_answer.text: Visiting with the preschool teacher after the farewell

correct_answers.text: Visiting with the preschool teacher after the farewell

questions.explanation: Preschool children need help in transitioning and saying good-bye. Visits, phone calls, pictures, and letters can often be helpful, and are certainly more helpful than trying to enforce a 'clean break.'

questions.question_text: True or False: Psychiatric disorders such as schizophrenia, bipolar disorder and Tourette's syndrome (TS) appear to exhibit mendelian patterns of inheritance.
questions.explanation: Single gene disorders typically exhibit mendelian patterns of inheritance (dominant, recessive, or X-linked). The psychiatric disorders listed in the options cannot be accounted for by the transmission of a single gene.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT one of the diagnostic criteria for gender identity disorder (GID)?

options.text: The disturbance is not concurrent with a physical intersex condition
A strong and persistent cross-gender identification
Persistent discomfort with his or her sex preference
The disturbance causes clinically significant distress and impairment in social, occupational, or other important areas of functioning

correct_answer.text: Persistent discomfort with his or her sex preference

correct_answers.text: Persistent discomfort with his or her sex preference

questions.explanation: The child has discomfort for his or her own sex, not the sex of his preference.

questions.question_text: In the treatment of selective mutism, introducing the child gradually and systematically into situations in which the child already speaks is an example of:
In which part of the brain are about half of all noradrenergic neurons located?
questions.explanation: The remaining noradrenergic neurons are distributed in the tegmental region.

questions.question_text: A developmental pediatrician is asked to evaluate a 24-month-old girl referred for regression in development. Her parents describe normal prenatal and perinatal development before recent loss of purposeful hand movements. DNA analysis is likely to reveal?

options.text: Disruption at the 'fragile' site on the X chromosome

questions.explanation: Rett syndrome is a disorder within the autism spectrum with prevalence of 1 in 10,000. Affected children achieve normal developmental milestones within the first year of life. One of the first clinical findings is the loss of purposeful hand movements. Others soon emerge including loss of speech, growth retardation with microcephaly, ataxia and severe disruption in normal cognitive functioning. The disorder almost exclusively affects girls.

questions.question_text: The 5-year training program in pediatrics, general psychiatry, and child and adolescent psychiatry, better known as the 'Triple Board' began as a pilot training experiment in which year?
questions.explanation: The Triple Board was approved as a combined residency on a nationwide basis in 1992.

questions.question_text: Which of the following marks the start of adolescence?
questions.explanation: Adrenarche, the steady increase in adrenally produced androgens, begins as early as age 6 to 8 years old and leads to increased skeletal growth and the initial appearance of body hair. Gonadarche occurs when the pulsatile release of gonadotropin-releasing hormone produces increased pituitary release of follicle-stimulating hormone and luteinizing hormone, in turn, driving the production of gonadal hormones (testosterone in boys, estrogen in girls). Gonadarche is the official marker of puberty.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is TRUE?

options.text: Two-thirds of adults with autism achieve independence
By school age, many children with autism become more socially responsive
Language skills of children with autism never improve
By age 2, many children with autism show clear repetitive behaviors
Early intervention studies show no improvement in independent functioning

correct_answer.text: By school age, many children with autism become more socially responsive

correct_answers.text: By school age, many children with autism become more socially responsive

questions.explanation: Children with autism do show some improvements in language and social responsiveness with age and early intervention. Detection by age 2 years can be difficult as the classic signs of autism tend to be detected around age 3 to 4 years. The majority of adults with autism do not achieve personal and occupational independence.

questions.question_text: In a survey of 785 adolescent and adult females, which ethnic group had the highest rate of anorexia nervosa?

options.text: None, they were all found to be within the mean

correct_answer.text: None, they were all found to be within the mean

correct_answers.text: None, they were all found to be within the mean

questions.explanation: In a large cross-sectional study no differences among Asians, African-Americans, Hispanics, and whites were found in mean rates of any eating disorder symptoms.

questions.question_text: What is the lifetime prevalence of bipolar disorder in the offspring of parents with bipolar disorder?
In McHugh and Slavney's four perspectives in psychiatric assessment that serves as an alternative to the biopsychosocial approach to formulation, which component addresses 'what a patient is'?
questions.explanation: The component of dimension refers to the range of psychological vulnerabilities and their severity in a presenting patient.

questions.question_text: In the study of sexual orientation, what part of the brain, in both animals and humans, has received particular interest?
Which of the following elements compose psychic reality?
questions.explanation: Regardless of whether these phenomena accurately represent the external world, they all are components of psychic reality.

questions.question_text: Each of these is a model for psychiatric consultation to pediatrics EXCEPT:
True or False: Video surveillance of the mother and the child in the hospital has proved to be helpful in diagnosing Munchhausen syndrome by proxy.
questions.explanation: A retrospective review of 41 cases in which covert video surveillance was used to investigate a possible diagnosis of Munchhausen syndrome by proxy in a pediatric hospital found that 23 diagnoses were actually confirmed. Of these 23, covert video surveillance was seen as crucial to making the diagnosis in 13 (56%) and supportive of the diagnosis in five (28%).

questions.question_text: True or False: According to International Classification of Diseases (ICD)-10, conduct disorder is not diagnosed if attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) symptoms are present.
questions.explanation: This would warrant a diagnosis of hyperkinetic conduct disorder.

questions.question_text: ALL of the following may be a medical consequence of taking anabolic steroids EXCEPT:

options.text: Development of male sexual characteristics in women

questions.explanation: Steroid use can result in shrinking testicles.

questions.question_text: When is the best time to begin discussing with a child that he or she was adopted?

options.text: When they are in late elementary school
When they ask whether they are adopted

questions.explanation: There is no set age, but most clinicians and adoptive professionals recommend telling a child early. Giving children information early, even before they can comprehend wholly the information, establishes a process of discussion and openness that leads to developmentally appropriate conversations.

questions.question_text: True or False: It is not unethical to use human subjects as a means to accomplish goals of research.
questions.explanation: What is prohibited is the use of persons solely as a means to this end.

questions.question_text: Posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) symptoms in children are more likely to occur when there are additional stressors after the traumatic event including ALL of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Reexperiencing the trauma is one of the symptoms of posttraumatic stress disorder.

questions.question_text: In interpersonal psychotherapy for depressed adolescents (IPT-A), just as in the adult version (IPT), there are four identified problem areas upon which the therapy can focus. These four areas include ALL of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: When there appears to be two problem areas for the course of interpersonal therapy, the therapist should identify a primary and possibly secondary area of focus.

questions.question_text: In any given year, how many children under 15 will have epilepsy?
questions.explanation: 300,000 children under 15 have epilepsy, which represents 1 in 200. Each year 7 in 10,000 children under 15 will develop recurrent seizures.

questions.question_text: Which of the following sources is the BEST option for a forensic psychiatrist seeking ethical guidelines for a forensic evaluation?

options.text: American Academy of Child & Adolescent Psychiatry
American Academy of Psychiatry and the Law

correct_answer.text: American Academy of Psychiatry and the Law

correct_answers.text: American Academy of Psychiatry and the Law

questions.explanation: Forensic psychiatrists should be aware of the ethical guidelines provided by the American Academy of Psychiatry and the Law, which are more specific to forensics than those of the other organizations.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT TRUE of children with childhood onset schizophrenia?

options.text: Higher rates of early social abnormalities
Higher rates of early language impairment
Higher rates of early motor abnormalities

questions.explanation: Patients with childhood onset schizophrenia present with higher rates of early language, social, and motor developmental abnormalities.

questions.question_text: At higher doses, venlafaxine can be associated with the risk of which side effect in a dose-dependent relationship?
questions.explanation: This side effect can occur with doses greater than 150 mg daily.

questions.question_text: Acute depression, intense anger, anxiety about future relationships, and social withdrawal can be characteristic of which group experiencing parental divorce?
questions.explanation: Adolescents will also accelerate separation and individuation from the family.

questions.question_text: Children acquire skills best when:

options.text: They are under stress or trauma
Caregivers present them with tasks that are slightly too difficult to accomplish independently

correct_answer.text: Caregivers present them with tasks that are slightly too difficult to accomplish independently

correct_answers.text: Caregivers present them with tasks that are slightly too difficult to accomplish independently

questions.explanation: Children acquire skills best when caregivers present them with tasks that are just a bit too difficult for them to accomplish independently, but are possible with appropriate assistance.

questions.question_text: Multisystemic therapy, and the home-based service model within which it is delivered, differs from intensive, home-based family preservation programs that employ the crisis intervention model in several ways. These differences include:

options.text: An assigned family aid who is from the same community as the family
Individual treatment of each family member
Master's level clinicians supervised by doctoral-level clinicians

correct_answer.text: Master's level clinicians supervised by doctoral-level clinicians

correct_answers.text: Master's level clinicians supervised by doctoral-level clinicians

questions.explanation: Doctoral-level clinicians trained in evidence-based practice supervise master's level clinicians.

questions.question_text: In defining the clinical skills essential for infant assessment, three techniques are central. Which of the following is NOT one of the techniques?

options.text: Synthesis of the information gathered during the evaluation
Observation of children and caregiver–child interactions

questions.explanation: Although these three skills are important for medical diagnosis in general, they have special significance in the assessment of infants as elaborated in Chapter 4.2.1.

questions.question_text: A child with deafness is likely to experience delays in ALL of the following areas EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: There is minimal motor delay, although delay linked to balance may occur.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a side effect of FK506, an immunosuppressant?
questions.explanation: FK506 is metabolized by the P450 system.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is most likely to be a direct prevention-minded treatment?
questions.explanation: In direct prevention-minded treatment, the intervention involves other family members as part of the treatment for the primary patient.

questions.question_text: A survey conducted by the National Association of State Fire Marshals in the late 1990s determined that children were responsible for roughly how many fires set annually?
questions.explanation: The fire-settings cause more than $250 million in property damage.

questions.question_text: True or False: According to available evidence, group cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) involving other family members is as effective as individual CBT.
As a child psychiatrist, when you receive a subpoena you should provide any documents requested:

options.text: If there is a court order to release the information
If the patient (or guardian) who holds the privilege to the health information has consented to its release
As soon as possible, as a court order is presumed in the subpoena

questions.explanation: The patient has to waive confidentiality or the court has to provide an order.

questions.question_text: True or False: In the group of individuals with mental retardation who have no known 'organic' cause, disproportionately more persons are poor, from minority backgrounds, and of low intelligence quotient (IQ) parents.
questions.explanation: In years past, the terms sociocultural or cultural–familial retardation reflected the view that nonorganic mental retardation (MR) stemmed from environmental deprivation.

questions.question_text: True or False: In middle and high school students with ADHD, the inattentive subtype is more common.
True or False: Boys with gender identity disorder (GID) seem to have an aversion for rough and tumble play.
questions.explanation: This is one of the descriptions within criterion B for gender identity disorder in the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM).

questions.question_text: Drummond conducted the first systematic follow-up of girls with GID, evaluating 25 girls with a mean age of 8.8 years with a follow-up mean of 23.2 years. What conclusion was found?
questions.explanation: Two of them had homosexual orientation; the third was asexual.

questions.question_text: In contrast to the more clinically oriented, categorical approach, multivariate or dimensional approaches to diagnosis offer ALL of the following advantages in the diagnosis of children and adolescents EXCEPT:

options.text: They assess various behaviors and dimensions of behavior rather than single pathognomonic features
They encompass symptom coding in other than a dichotomous fashion
They utilize various rating scales and checklists based on self, parent, and teacher reports, or direct observation
They consider a dichotomous understanding of psychopathology

correct_answer.text: They consider a dichotomous understanding of psychopathology

correct_answers.text: They consider a dichotomous understanding of psychopathology

questions.explanation: Categorical approaches are dichotomous in nature: either you have the disorder or you do not, whereas multivariate approaches are dimensional.

questions.question_text: ALL of these situations represent the potential establishment of a doctor–patient relationship with its ensuing fiduciary and legal obligations EXCEPT:

options.text: Responding to a nonpatient's e-mail with therapeutic advice
Therapeutic advice given to an acquaintance at a dinner party
Setting up of an appointment with a prospective patient, whom you have never seen, by the office staff for an initial evaluation
Responding to a prospective patient's e-mail with a referral to someone in the patient's geographic area
Working with the parents of a child in separate sessions without the child

correct_answer.text: Responding to a prospective patient's e-mail with a referral to someone in the patient's geographic area

correct_answers.text: Responding to a prospective patient's e-mail with a referral to someone in the patient's geographic area

questions.explanation: In working with parents or families, the physician may be viewed as taking on a doctor–patient with each parent or family member.

questions.question_text: The Brazelton Neonatal Behavioral Assessment Scale, second edition, a neonatal assessment test, is intended to assess ALL of the following capacities in the neonate EXCEPT:

options.text: Adjustment to the ex utero environment
Ability to respond to the stress of labor and delivery
Whether the neonate can be weaned from supplemental oxygen

correct_answer.text: Whether the neonate can be weaned from supplemental oxygen

correct_answers.text: Whether the neonate can be weaned from supplemental oxygen

questions.explanation: The Brazelton Neonatal Behavioral Assessment Scale, second edition, is designed for use with neonates of 37 to 44 weeks' gestational age who do not need mechanical supports or supplemental oxygen.

questions.question_text: Prior to initiating a trial of lithium, a child may warrant which of the following?
questions.explanation: The physician should also obtain creatinine levels and thyroid indices.

questions.question_text: How does parental education relate to children's school achievement?

options.text: Parental education is not related to children's school achievement
Directly, through parental evaluation of the teaching environment
Indirectly, through parental knowledge of discipline
Directly, through parents' drive to succeed
Indirectly, though reading and providing a warm and supportive environment

correct_answer.text: Indirectly, though reading and providing a warm and supportive environment

correct_answers.text: Indirectly, though reading and providing a warm and supportive environment

questions.explanation: Parental education is related to children's achievement in both white and African-American families.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statistics would most likely be used in a randomized experimental study?
questions.explanation: Randomized experimental studies utilize difference inferential statistics such as analysis of variance and t-tests.

questions.question_text: True or False: Fluoxetine has a metabolite that is psychoactive.
questions.explanation: Fluoxetine has an active metabolite, norfluoxetine, with an elimination half-life of 7 to 14 days.

questions.question_text: The concerns of young children about privacy are quite different from older children and adolescents. Which TWO of the following notions of privacy are the first to develop in young children?
questions.explanation: Territorial privacy ('This is my room.') and possessional privacy ('This is my bike.') develop in children prior to informational privacy, which involves concerns about others' knowledge of one's activities, interests, and associations.

questions.question_text: The direct and indirect cost of mental illness for the total population of the United States was estimated in 1996 to be what amount?
ALL of the following should be considered when a child presents with enuresis EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Option D provides a normal range for thyroid-stimulating hormone.

questions.question_text: The period of the day that is the time of greatest risk for youth-on-youth violence during weekdays occurs between:

options.text: Early morning and the start of school
End of the school day and early evening

correct_answer.text: End of the school day and early evening

correct_answers.text: End of the school day and early evening

questions.explanation: On nonschool days, however, the pattern of violent crime is more akin to the timing for adult offenders.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements likely represents the better approach to managing an aggressive patient in the emergency room?

options.text: 'You will not use vulgar language here'
Firmly but gently say: 'You are here for a psychiatric evaluation and you will not leave until it is completed'
'You have been here a while, would you like something to eat or drink?'
'Have you thought about what your mother goes through?'

correct_answer.text: 'You have been here a while, would you like something to eat or drink?'

correct_answers.text: 'You have been here a while, would you like something to eat or drink?'

questions.explanation: Offering something to eat can be an effective tool, if appropriate; how-ever, the main point here is that all other options represent directive or controlling statements, which are apt to be counterproductive.

questions.question_text: According to the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM)-IV-TR, a person with a diagnosis of mild mental retardation would have which of the following?
questions.explanation: Various levels of MR are specified in the DSM-IV-TR: mild (IQ 50–70), moderate (IQ 35–49), severe (IQ 20–34), and profound (IQ < 20).

questions.question_text: True or False: There have been two randomized, placebo-controlled trials for selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors in the treatment of trichotillomania. At least one trial demonstrated significant improvement over placebo.
questions.explanation: There was no difference between placebo and active treatment. Open-label studies report rates of improvement of 30% to 60%.

questions.question_text: The diagnostic criteria for bulimia include ALL of the following EXCEPT:

options.text: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behavior to prevent weight gain, such as self-induced vomiting; misuse of laxatives, diuretics, or other medications; fasting; excessive exercise
These symptoms occur at least twice a week on average and persist for at least 3 months
The disturbance does not occur exclusively during episodes of anorexia nervosa

questions.explanation: Body mass index is not part of the diagnostic criteria for bulimia.

questions.question_text: When a credible and appropriate referral to mental health services is offered by a pediatrician, how many families follow-up with a mental health clinician?
questions.explanation: Less than half follow-up. Generally, uncomplicated attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) can be managed in the primary care setting but pediatric depression and other disorders are generally seen as the purview of mental health specialists.

questions.question_text: The first structured parent-report diagnostic interview specifically designed for preschool-age children became available in which year?
questions.explanation: This question is intended to impress upon you the very little research on preschool psychopathology as reflected by the dearth of diagnostic interviews for this population.

questions.question_text: Which edition of the DSM officially introduced the category of conduct disorder?
True or False: Boys have greater innate capability for mathematics than girls do.
questions.explanation: The belief that boys are more mathematically capable than girls has been demonstrated to be more an effect of socialization than innate capability.

questions.question_text: True or False: Medically unexplained physical symptoms and complaints are exceptionally common in children and adolescents.
questions.explanation: Approximately half of preschool and school age children report at least one somatic complaint in the previous 2 weeks.

questions.question_text: There are approximately 7,000 child and adolescent psychiatrists in the United States. What is the estimated number of psychiatrists needed to provide care for seriously psychiatrically ill children and youth?
questions.explanation: This statistic underlines the great need to recruit and train more physicians in child and adolescent psychiatry, especially to underserved areas.

ALL of the following individual risk factors are associated with the development of disruptive behavior disorders EXCEPT:
Which of the following represents a well-known epidemiological survey in the United States?
questions.explanation: This survey occurred in North Carolina.

questions.question_text: ALL of these are generally sound principles in the management of functional somatic symptoms EXCEPT:

options.text: Avoid communicating any sense of unease about the diagnosis
The judicious use of placebo treatment can help limit doctor shopping
Do not emphasize that functional somatic symptoms are reactions to adversity and stress
Once the diagnosis is made additional medical workup should be avoided in the absence of new information or change in clinical status
When the diagnostic formulation is clear it should be discussed frankly with the patient and family together

questions.question_text: True or False: In custody evaluations, it is helpful to have had a prior treatment relationship with the child.
questions.explanation: The forensic evaluator must avoid conflicts of interest. Page 1008.

questions.question_text: ALL of the following are psychosocial strategies in making aggressive behavior in children irrelevant by changing antecedents EXCEPT:

options.text: Modifying demands and ways of communicating them
Restricting access to peers who promote misconduct

questions.explanation: Option C is a strategy on how to make aggressive behavior ineffective by changing consequences. Page 477.

questions.question_text: True or False: In infant/toddler screening tests used to pick out children who are developmentally at risk, the test's sensitivity is considered more important than its specificity.
questions.explanation: Although it is desirable to reduce both types of errors, sensitivity appears more important than specificity in screening tests as false positives can be identified with follow-up testing. (Specificity reduces the false-positive rate, whereas sensitivity reduces the false-negative rate.) Page 320.

questions.question_text: When were juvenile courts first created?
questions.explanation: Juvenile courts were created to focus on the rehabilitation (rather than punishment) of juvenile delinquents, thus differentiating them from adult courts. Page 999.

questions.question_text: Fragile X is a problem of mRNA ______?
questions.explanation: There is a mutation in the protein that regulates translation of messages. Page 181.

questions.question_text: The involvement of mental health services, whether directly or indirectly, in school systems has become more prevalent over the years for ALL of the following reasons EXCEPT:

options.text: Federal education rights legislation led to the increasing identification of students with emotional and behavioral difficulties
Decreased psychiatric hospitalizations and residential placements, along with limited outpatient mental health resources, led to increased mental health utilization in schools
Increased social change and the recognition of problem behaviors in the 1960s led schools to turn to mental health clinicians for guidance
Refugee students were displaced after World War II, and school-based interventions to assist teachers with these students were developed
No Child Left Behind legislation mandated the early identification and treatment of children with emotional disturbances in school

correct_answer.text: No Child Left Behind legislation mandated the early identification and treatment of children with emotional disturbances in school

correct_answers.text: No Child Left Behind legislation mandated the early identification and treatment of children with emotional disturbances in school

questions.explanation: No Child Left Behind requires intervention earlier for those students not progressing as expected, and not identification and treatment of emotional disturbances per se. Page 981.

questions.question_text: In the biopsychosocial model of formulation, which of the following components belong in the social realm?
questions.explanation: Refer to Table 4.2.6.2. Page 378.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following antipsychotics was the first used in children with severe behavioral disturbances?
questions.explanation: Although its use has declined due to newer atypical antipsychotics, chlorpromazine is still routinely used for the acute management of agitation or aggression. Page 776.

questions.question_text: True or False: Slightly higher dosing of valproate is required when transitioning to the extended release formulation.
questions.explanation: Between an 8% and 20% increase is required. Page 771.

questions.question_text: Unlike an aphasia arising from focal lesions, an aphasia from the Landau-Kleffner syndrome:

options.text: Is the result of right hemisphere damage
Usually has its onset after 13 years of age
Is more common in girls than boys
Severely affects reading and writing, but usually spares comprehension

questions.explanation: Landau-Kleffner syndrome (LKS) usually has its onset between 3 and 6 years of age, although it can occur any time between 2 and 13 years. In general, prognosis is worse the earlier the onset of the syndrome, which is more common in boys than in girls. Unlike aphasias associated with focal lesions, LKS may result in a permanent aphasia. Another difference is that comprehension is more severely affected in LKS and reading and writing may be relatively spared. Page 423.

questions.question_text: Optimally, screening the victims of a disaster for possible mental health problems should be done:
questions.explanation: Page 732.

questions.question_text: Melanie Klein, considered one of the founders of child psychoanalysis, coined the term 'play analysis.' ALL of the following statements describe her therapeutic approach with children EXCEPT:

options.text: Encouraging early and deep interpretations in therapeutic methodology
Emphasizing the ego mechanisms of defense against intolerable affect states
Emphasizing the child's play as equivalent to free association in adult analysis
Minimizing the analyst's contact with parents and teachers

correct_answer.text: Emphasizing the ego mechanisms of defense against intolerable affect states

correct_answers.text: Emphasizing the ego mechanisms of defense against intolerable affect states

questions.explanation: Anna Freud studied the ego mechanisms of defense. Page 827.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements best defines the elimination half-life ( t1/2)?

options.text: The time required for the concentration of a drug to increase by one-half
The time required for one-half of the psychoactive component of a drug to be made inactive
The time required for the body to metabolize one-half of the amount of a drug
The time required for the concentration of a drug to decrease by one-half

correct_answer.text: The time required for the concentration of a drug to decrease by one-half

correct_answers.text: The time required for the concentration of a drug to decrease by one-half

questions.explanation: In clinical practice, the elimination half-life is usually assessed by measuring the decay of plasma or serum drug concentration. Page 743.

questions.question_text: True or False: Lamotrigine undergoes only a Phase I metabolic reaction.
questions.explanation: Lamotrigine undergoes only a Phase II metabolic reaction as it is transformed only by glucuronidation. Page 750.

questions.question_text: True or False: With regard to therapy group and meeting protocol, omission of any segment of the protocol, regardless of how justified such an omission might seem by events of the moment, will always diminish the group's trust in its leaders and in the structure of the group.
questions.explanation: Page 846.

questions.question_text: Which criterion of OCD in DSM-IV-TR does not apply to children?

options.text: The obsessions or compulsions are time consuming (take more than 1 hour a day)
The behaviors or mental acts are aimed at preventing or reducing distress
At some point, the person has recognized that the obsessions or compulsions are excessive or unreasonable
There is no criterion, which does not also apply to children
The person recognizes that the obsessional thoughts are the product of his or her own mind

correct_answer.text: At some point, the person has recognized that the obsessions or compulsions are excessive or unreasonable

correct_answers.text: At some point, the person has recognized that the obsessions or compulsions are excessive or unreasonable

questions.explanation: Criterion B. Page 549.

questions.question_text: True or False: The successful treatment of adolescent anxiety with selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors may reduce the risk for subsequent depression.
questions.explanation: This question shows one link between anxiety and depression, and a possible preventative approach to adolescent psychiatry. Page 506.

questions.question_text: Institutional deprivation syndrome can result in symptoms similar to which of the following diagnoses?
questions.explanation: Although these symptoms (hyperactivity and inattention) are not part of reactive attachment disorder, some have suggested that the inattention and overactivity seen in children with a history of institutionalization and attachment disturbances may reflect an 'institutional deprivation syndrome.' Page 714.
